revisions: Before the first full-size run, after a 5-query trial: the two weak-retriever comparisons went from strict at every K_c to non-strict at every K_c and strict at the smallest, because where the gate removes nothing both regimes are exactly zero; and the policy checks gained the not-testable guard, because the trial's D_q was smaller than the outsider budget, so every policy promoted all of it.

After the first full-size run: 'weak_retriever_gate_costs_more' compared the NET per-query gate effect, DCG(pi_act) - DCG(pi_no1), and failed at K_c=1000 (weak retriever +0.021 vs strong stages 0.000). The net effect adds two opposite channels: the loss on documents the gate excludes (cost) and the gain for survivors shielded from strong competitors (protection). A weak retriever's gate has far more of both (K_c=1000: cost -3.710 vs 0.000, protection +3.732 vs 0.000), and they nearly cancel. Replaced by 'weak_retriever_gate_cost_higher', on the cost alone; the net effect and both channels stay in the stage-effects table.
